source: O.W.L Observe / Win / Learn forms — every submission to date

observe.label: Job scope completed safely and as planned
Atmospheric hazards tested prior to first break
Evaluation and discussion of life saving rules
Safety control measures were utilized(ex. Hot work/LOTO/Confined Space)
Communicated issues with PIC and corrected before work began

win.label: Strong communication between Canon technician and crews
Strong communication between Canon technician and PIC
All personnel on location work together effectively to mitigate any hazards
Life saving rules understood and discussed with all personnel on site
Crew verified conditions in the field instead of relying on paperwork
Standard rig up completed correctly with no rework required

improveQuotes.text: Utilize a cheater pipe from the beginning stages of the job instead of “bouncing” on the pipe wrench and risking a potential fall.
Set up a completely sealed exclusion zone — not just cones — because some people felt entitled to walk right in. I had to kick them out.
Do a pre-task briefing beforehand to ensure everyone is on the same page on job progression.
Language barrier is a concern — roustabouts speak and understand Spanish, not so good with English.
Interpret the Spanish side of the 12 Life-Saving Rules.
Add a brief refresher on offset frac protection criteria for new crew members before the job.
A crew member showed up with an invalid fit-test card — we used someone else to break containment and flagged the card.
Always check before starting work to make sure no casing valves are leaking — check the bleeders.
Verify all equipment is actually going to show up — the vac truck didn’t, and it made a big mess cleaning tanks out.
More atmospheric tests while the crew is working, while staying out of the line of fire.
